title: Surgical Fine-Tuning Improves Adaptation to Distribution Shifts
mechanism: Tuning only a subset of layers matches or beats full fine-tuning; the best block depends on shift type (input-level shifts favour early layers); tuning more parameters on small data forgets pretrained information.
adaptation: Arms: train stem+layer1-2 with layer3-4 frozen at ImageNet; and the reverse. Decoder always trained. E1 shift (scuff streaks, half-cut layout, contrast) is input-level, so early-layer tuning is predicted to help E1.
evidence: Seven real-world tasks, three shift types; first-layer tuning best for image corruptions (abstract).
min_experiment: Two arms vs SUP100-PF on module-grouped 5-fold CV, 2 seeds, then 5 seeds for the winner. Metric: CV inactive IoU and crack relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU. Kill if neither arm beats PF on CV by +0.01 inactive IoU or +0.005 relF1@2.
prior_overlap: Partial: PF freezes the whole encoder for 1k steps only. Block-wise permanent freezing never run.

alt_notes.adaptation: Arms: tune stem + layer1-2 with layer3-4 frozen at ImageNet, and the reverse; decoder always trained. E1's shifts (scuff, half-cut, contrast) are input-level, so early-layer tuning is the prediction.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: two surgical freezes, 5-fold CV x 2 seeds, then 5 seeds on full train. Baseline: SUP100-PF. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU, test crack relF1@2. Kill: neither freeze beats PF on E1 by +0.02 relF1@2 or +0.03 inactive IoU.
